notes: \cpara{Two epigraphs: \textsc{Lamia}, Part II, lines 229 to 233, and a sentence from the Feynman footnote quoted in ``Savanna Poets.''}
\cpara{Asks what, besides rainbows, goes into Keats's ``dull catalogue of common things.''}

\cpara{Answers: whatever is known, knowable or lawful, ``in a word, real.'' The reading has support in the passage, which says the rainbow entered the catalogue because ``We know her woof'' and complains that philosophy will ``Conquer all mysteries by rule and line.''}
\cpara{The consequence, as a joke: on that standard everything will disappoint, either by not existing or by being real.}
\cpara{The thesis, stated as a conditional. It is the ``usual reply'' that ``Explaining vs.\ Explaining Away'' promised to expand.}

\cpara{Says the rainbow's sin was having a scientific explanation, and offers three suspicions about Keats, each marked ``I suspect'': that he did not know the explanation himself, that being told someone else knew was too much, and that even explicability in principle would have been. The evidence about what Keats knew is discussed in the notes on ``Fake Reductionism.''}
\cpara{Restates ``Mysterious Answers to Mysterious Questions'' and ``Probability is in the Mind'': ignorance is a fact about the mind, and ``A blank map does not correspond to a blank territory.''}
\cpara{The step: since nothing that exists is mysterious in itself, everything real is ``liable'' to end up in the catalogue.}

\cpara{The choice: care about real, explicable things, or suffer an ennui that cannot be resolved. Given the premise that Keats's standard makes every real thing dull in time, the second option follows for anyone who keeps that standard.}
\cpara{Rules out a third option, self-deception, for the reader, with a link to ``Doublethink (Choosing to be Biased).''}
\cpara{Recasts scientists' fascination with pocket lint and bird droppings as the right response to the choice.}
\cpara{Concludes, with three qualifiers (``You might say,'' ``some,'' ``in principle''), that scientists are people able to enjoy the real universe.}
